text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000112 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, but with only one documented 99215 the records are too thin to tell upcoding from a complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel is genuinely weighted toward multimorbid patients, and most 99215s fall on patients with four or more conditions (e.g., C0062101, C0062292). That is consistent with complex care, but the 99215 share runs roughly double the all-provider share in every condition band, including 0–2 conditions, and the overall mix leans heavily on 99214. Together that pattern is consistent with a level shift across the board, not just a sicker panel. The low-complexity sample includes 99215s that are hard to square with the diagnoses, such as C0063125 (no chronic conditions, upper respiratory infection J06.9), C0063236 (same patient, follow-up Z09) and C0062089 (22-year-old, back pain). Documentation cannot settle the question: records cover about 1% of claims and only one 99215 (C0063343, documented high MDM), so the clean 0% unsupported rate and the absence of no-lab mismatches carry little weight. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s and a larger random set of 99215 and 99214 claims, then compare documented MDM and time against the billed level."}
